name: cloud-sync-coordination-hazard
question: Is this project's coordination store inside a cloud-synced folder, where a background sync client can silently discard a write the mkdir lock believed it had serialized?
cost_provenance: Pure path-string inspection of the resolved project root plus an optional Windows attribute probe -- no directory walking, no network. 200ms is a pessimistic shell cold-start allowance; measured well under 100ms on win32 2026-07-19.

schema.hosted: boolean (true iff the project root resolves under a recognized cloud-sync provider path)
schema.provider: string|null (OneDrive|Dropbox|Google Drive|iCloud Drive; null when not hosted or undeterminable)
schema.root: string|null (the resolved project root inspected; null when undeterminable -> graceful absence)
schema.matched_segment: string|null (the path segment that triggered the match, for auditability)
schema.at_risk_paths: array of strings (coordination-store paths that exist under the hosted root)
schema.briefing: string (empty when not hosted -> session-start suppresses the line)

_briefingForms.hosted: "coordination store is inside <provider> (<segment>) -- concurrent writes to active-sessions.json / touches.json / channels can be silently reconciled away below the lock (DISC-CSI-25). Prefer a local path for this project, or avoid concurrent PODS work here."

source_priority: env ULDF_CLOUD_SYNC_PROVIDERS (comma-separated segment list, overrides defaults)

fallback: Run `pwd -W` (Git Bash) or `(Get-Location).Path` (PowerShell) and look for a OneDrive/Dropbox/Google Drive segment. If present, the project's .claude/collaboration/ and .claude/session-state/ are on synced storage.
graceful_absence: When the project root cannot be resolved, the oracle emits hosted=false with an empty briefing rather than guessing. A false 'you are safe' is the failure mode to avoid least here: the oracle is a tripwire, not a guarantee, and its silence means 'no recognized provider segment', never 'verified safe'.

design_lineage: disk-artifact-bloat -- same cheap every-session environment tripwire shape, empty-briefing-suppresses-line discipline
segments/-ldis/spec_lock.md -- the pre-existing document-only mitigation of this same hazard class for the spec-edit lock
provenance.note: Detection-first response to DISC-CSI-25 / DEFER-016 (DEC-188). The mkdir-based lock in registry-write.{sh,ps1} serializes processes on ONE machine's local filesystem view; it has no leverage over a sync client's after-the-fact reconciliation, which can discard a write that was verified locally at write-time. Observed live 2026-07-12: two writers appended to grant-requests.jsonl ~2 minutes apart, both verified written, and only one record survived. This oracle does NOT fix that -- it makes the exposure visible every session so a human can decide, and generates the evidence that would justify the far more invasive store-relocation option later.
